blocks.content: The Cartesian coordinate system establishes a fundamental bridge between algebra and geometry through numerical coordinates.

items: Frequently tested: Finding the ratio in which the y-axis or x-axis divides a given line segment by setting x=0 or y=0.
Coordinates of the centroid of a triangle with vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2), and (x3, y3) are ((x1+x2+x3)/3, (y1+y2+y3)/3).
Check for collinearity of three points using the area of a triangle formula being equal to zero.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Cartesian coordinate system divides a 2D plane into four distinct quadrants using two mutually perpendicular axes.
The Distance Formula calculates the straight-line distance between any two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) in a coordinate plane.
The Section Formula determines the coordinates of a point that divides a line segment joining two points in a given ratio m:n internally or externally.
The Midpoint Formula is a special case of the section formula where the ratio m:n is equal to 1:1.
